title: The philosopher Wittgenstein spent about a year designing one house’s door handles

cover.alt: The plain white cubic walls and tall, narrow windows of Haus Wittgenstein, a modernist townhouse in Vienna, with bare tree branches at one side.

body: In 1925 Margaret Stonborough-Wittgenstein commissioned a modernist townhouse in Vienna, and the architect Paul Engelmann drew the first design. Her brother Ludwig, the philosopher, joined the project in 1926 and soon became more its author than a helper. He fixated on windows, doors, doorknobs and radiators, demanding exact measurements: the door handles took about a year to design and the radiators another. The house was finished in December 1928, and the family spent that Christmas in it.

slides.alt: Close-up of a plain, slightly worn brass door handle with a simple bend, above a keyhole on a beige door inside Haus Wittgenstein.
slides.caption: One of the door handles in Haus Wittgenstein. Its design took about a year.

slides.label: how much he had one ceiling raised
slides.text: Just enough to give the room the proportions he wanted.

slides.question: Each window had a metal screen, moved by a pulley Wittgenstein designed. How heavy was each screen?
slides.explanation: About 150 kg each. One architect on the job, Jacques Groag, said the work was full of quarrels, ‘mostly between me and Wittgenstein’.

slides.text: Even though I admired the house very much, I always knew that I neither wanted to, nor could, live in it myself.

events.text: Finished in time for a family Christmas
Russian soldiers use it as barracks and stables
Sold to a developer for demolition
Saved and made a national monument

slides.question: What has the house been used for since 1975?
slides.explanation: Since 1975 it has housed the cultural department of the Bulgarian Embassy in Vienna.
